title: a crossing's proven_by is a posix path, written and read
intention: proven_by_since_buildme returns posix paths whatever separator the journal stored, and the crossing writes proven_by with forward slashes.
why: Measured 2026-11-12 on akiendell: orchestrator's Linux run of cairn test --hollow refused 15 Windows tickets because proven_by held backslash paths; tickets/3854f1aee8eb-*.log.jsonl proven_by stores cairn\\devices\\sudo_relay\\proofs\\test_sudo_relay.py
traces_to: Law 3 and Law 8: a proof path a Linux reader cannot match is evidence no peer can lean on; Law 7: the stored record is kept as written, the reader fixes the reading.
how: In cairn/tools/base/crossings.py _norm_proof replaces backslashes with forward slashes before the repo-prefix strip (so a backslash absolute path under the repo also strips). In cairn/tools/base/cross.py the proven_by list is written through the same posix conversion. Red-first proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_crossing_proven_by_is_posix.py feeds a fixture journal record carrying a backslash path and asserts the posix path back, and calls the crossing's write path and asserts no backslash is stored.

clauses.claim: a journal record whose proven_by carries backslashes reads back from proven_by_since_buildme as the posix path
the crossing writes proven_by with forward slashes, so a Windows crossing stores no backslash

decisions.text: D1: the fix at cairn/tools/base/crossings.py, cairn/tools/base/cross.py
D2: one proof, one tooth per clause; red first.

The verdict instrument was a bare proof path (exit 126, not a command). Redrafted every criterion's instrument as 'bin/cairn test cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_crossing_proven_by_is_posix.py' and re-charted on Linux (validate-20261113T015311-94be100ee8f5); the build itself is unchanged.
